# v0.9.23 - Seafile Professional and the Review Backlog

## What's Changed in v0.9.23

A release for Seafile Professional and for the last review round's backlog. On Pro a file read under a folder that does not exist answers 403 (one level missing) or a 500 page (two or more), where Community Edition answers 404, so the first push to a new path stopped at its first read (issue 6). The helper now asks the folder's listing, which says 404 on both, and only then reads the file as "not there yet"; a real permission refusal still stops the push and now says to check the folder's permissions. The real-server suite now runs in CI against throwaway CE and Pro 13.0.29 containers, and passed by hand against both before that.

### Fixed
- **From the pre-release review**: a new file whose name differs from an indexed one only beyond ASCII case (`straße/` beside `strasse/`) is no longer dropped from a snapshot; a `--no-push` run remembers no setting; an LFS upload is proven by the listing; a ref the server lists but cannot serve is not overwritten; a repository folder moved in the web UI makes a fetch fail instead of pruning every tracking branch; a first push deletes only a copy its own mkdir made of one of the helper's own folders, and names any other.
- **The first push to a new path works on Seafile Professional** (issue 6). Measured on Pro and CE 13.0.29, for the library owner and a shared user, under every folder permission.
- **Two first pushes at once no longer leave an empty `.git-lock (1).d` behind.** Seafile numbers a duplicate folder before its extension, which the old check never matched.
- **`lfs-setup` keeps a library name with a space whole.** git-lfs splits the agent's arguments on whitespace (measured), so `seafile://My Library/...` reached the agent cut in two; it is now quoted, and a split one is refused.
- **A directory renamed by case is one directory in the snapshot** on both staging routes (Windows, macOS).
- **A clone that borrows objects (`alternates`) no longer skips a fetch's download**; `--payload-jobs N` retries a push-back at the level you typed; a small proxy limit tries the 4 MiB floor before giving up; an empty pack download is reported as empty.

### Added
- **`gc`, `gc --tail` and `repair` check the scratch space before downloading anything**, and say how much they need; `--allow-low-disk` starts anyway.

### Changed
- **On Seafile Professional, `gc` and `--payload-delete` refuse for an account that does not own the library**: a folder permission can hide refs from it (measured). `--allow-non-owner` / `--payload-allow-non-owner` override.
- **`--payload-delete` refuses clocks more than an hour apart**, not a day: a smaller step went unseen and shortened the grace period by as much.
- **A folder the account may not use now says so**: a 403 on a folder ends `This account may not see here` (or `write here`) and names the library's and the folder's permissions, instead of reading like a lock problem.
- **The advice to create folders by hand is gone**; it led to a ref made as a folder.
- **The snapshot tool picks its staging command by the work** (paths times index entries), not only the path count.
- **The docs say which servers are tested**: both editions of Seafile 13.0, in CI.

### Tests
- **The real-server workflow runs against CE and Pro containers** (public Pro image, trial licence, no secret), with a second account: folder permissions, group-shared and group-owned libraries, and two accounts racing a first push. A real-server run now refuses to start unless its helper processes log in to the same server as the test.
- `GRS_STUB_PRO=1` runs the whole stub suite against Pro's answers; `--status` and `--maintain` are tested to write nothing.

### Upgrading

Nothing about what is stored changes and no setting is renamed. Behaviours that may surface: `gc`, `gc --tail` and `repair` refuse when the temporary directory cannot hold about twice the packs (pass `--allow-low-disk`, or point `TMPDIR`/`TEMP` elsewhere), and the automatic tail merge skips; a repository set up with `lfs-setup` for a URL with a space fails loudly until `lfs-setup` is run again; a clone with `alternates` downloads packs a fetch used to skip; a `--no-push` snapshot remembers none of its flags; a push over a listed ref that cannot be read is refused. See `UPGRADING.md`.

The full list is in `CHANGELOG.md`.
